land.text: "the northern province of Sagaing of the Pinya kingdom", which "claimed all the way to the border of Manipur"

predecessors.note: Saw Yun, Thihathu's eldest son, governed Sagaing from 1314 and in 1315 "walked out of the Pinya Palace, never to return"; he "formally seceded in 1325". Cliopatria's Sagaing shape starts in 1326, after the formal secession.

land.text: "In 1365, Thado Minbya founded the kingdom of Ava and declared Sagaing and Pinya constituent countries of Ava"

successors.note: Thado Minbya, Sagaing's king from 1364, took Pinya in September 1364 and founded Ava in 1365 (Pinya page: the city of Ava proclaimed 26 February 1365; Sagaing page: inscription of 8 July 1365 as king of Ava). Ava's Cliopatria row begins in 1375 with the same 672 cells as Pinya of 1314.

capitals.name: Sagaing
capitals.note: The page names Sagaing as capital ("sacking both capitals of Sagaing and Pinya in succession", 1364) without separate dates; coordinates are the gazetteer's Sagaing. Thado Minbya's new city of Ava (Inwa) is the capital of the successor state.

rulers.name: Saw Yun
rulers.note: Page table: 1315-27; chronicles that date the revolt to 684 ME (1322-23) disagree, and an inscription has him founding Sagaing on 26 March 1316.

rulers.name: Thihapate
rulers.note: Page: "possibly" to 1364; he escaped the April 1364 sack and was later killed by his stepson Thado Minbya.

rulers.name: Thado Minbya
rulers.note: Page table: 1364-67; from 1365 king of Ava (reign continues past this state's end).

correction.text: "the northern province of Sagaing of the Pinya kingdom": the Cliopatria outline of 1326 held from 1315, contested with Pinya in 1315-1316 and autonomous under Pinya's nominal overlordship in 1317-1325

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts Sagaing in 1326, after the formal secession, but the page dates the kingdom "from 1315 to 1365" ("a small kingdom ruled by a junior branch of the Myinsaing dynasty"). Saw Yun "successfully fought for autonomy from his father King Thihathu in 1315-17"; "Sagaing formally seceded from Pinya in 1325 after Thihathu's death". The page's own footnotes disagree on the founding (inscription: 26 March 1316; earlier chronicles: revolt in 1322-23). The extent before 1325 is not on the page; the 1326 outline is used.

98,185 km2 (345 cells: Sagaing 124, Magway 88, Mandalay 82, Shan 50). The page gives no area; it says Sagaing "claimed all the way to the border of Manipur" while "its effective control may have been no more than half today's Sagaing Region" and was "without the Shan state of Kalay in the upper Chindwin region or anything beyond Tagaung", the northernmost fort being 225 km from Sagaing. The outline (bbox west to 94.3 E, north to 24.0 N) fits the claim and is probably about twice the effective area; kept as the claim. Tagaung, Mindon, Minbu and Pinle are named as neighbouring districts.

correction.text: unchanged outline for 1363 and until September 1364, when Thado Minbya "seized Pinya, and claimed himself king of Sagaing and Pinya"; from then the new keyframe sagaing-kingdom_1364 holds, to 1365

keyframe_review.note: Same outline as 1326 (345 cells). Cliopatria keeps it to 1374, but the page ends the state in 1365 ("from 1315 to 1365"); the Maw forces took the city in April 1364 ("In April 1364, Maw forces broke through, and entered the city"), without any recorded change of border.

correction.text: Sagaing and Pinya under one king: "In September 1364, Thado Minbya seized Pinya, and claimed himself king of Sagaing and Pinya"; Pinya less the Toungoo district lost in 1358

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the realm Thado Minbya held until he "founded the kingdom of Ava and declared Sagaing and Pinya constituent countries of Ava" in 1365. 345 + 262 cells (about 98,000 + 77,000 km2: shapes.csv gives 98,185 km2 for Sagaing's 345 cells and 95,056 km2 for Pinya's 324, of which 262 remain without Toungoo). The page gives no area for the union, and does not say whether Toungoo returned (the Pinya page says it "successfully broke away" in 1358).

region.text: "the northern province of Sagaing of the Pinya kingdom"

ledger.note: 1315: Prince Saw Yun walks out of the Pinya Palace and founds the kingdom of Sagaing. "In 1315, the teenage prince walked out of the Pinya Palace, never to return"; Sagaing was "a small kingdom ruled by a junior branch of the Myinsaing dynasty from 1315 to 1365". Footnotes give 26 March 1316 (inscription) and 1322-23 (chronicles) for the founding or revolt.

region.text: Sagaing, the northern province governed by Saw Yun

ledger.note: 1315: the war of autonomy with Pinya begins. Saw Yun "successfully fought for autonomy from his father King Thihathu in 1315-17"; the page names no battle.

region.text: Sagaing, the northern province governed by Saw Yun

ledger.note: 1317: Sagaing wins its autonomy. "Sagaing got a breather in 1317 when Toungoo and Taungdwin revolted"; the fight lasted "1315-17". Pinya counts Sagaing as its vassal until 1325 (see its ledger).

region.text: Pinya, seized by Thado Minbya in September 1364

ledger.note: September 1364: Thado Minbya takes Pinya. "In September 1364, Thado Minbya seized Pinya, and claimed himself king of Sagaing and Pinya." Maw forces had taken Sagaing city in April 1364; Thihapate "escaped but was later killed by his stepson Thado Minbya".

region.text: Sagaing and Pinya, constituent countries of Ava

ledger.note: 1365: Thado Minbya founds the kingdom of Ava. "In 1365, Thado Minbya founded the kingdom of Ava and declared Sagaing and Pinya constituent countries of Ava"; the inscription of 8 July 1365 already calls him king of Ava.

wars.name: Saw Yun's war of autonomy (Sagaing)

zones.text: Sagaing, the northern province governed by Saw Yun

wars.outcome: Saw Yun "successfully fought for autonomy from his father King Thihathu in 1315-17"; formal secession in 1325.
wars.note: My label; the page names no battle or treaty. Toungoo and Taungdwin revolted in 1317, relieving Sagaing.

wars.name: Sagaing-Pinya hostilities and the 1351 truce
wars.outcome: Shwetaungtet's expedition of 1339 to Mindon, "inside Pinya territory", brought Saw Yun's children back to Sagaing; "the situation turned cold again in 1340"; Princess Soe Min was sent in the 1350s to seek a truce with Kyawswa II, and the Pinya page has a truce with the northern rival in 1351.
wars.note: My label; neither page describes a battle or a moved border. The 1356-57 marriage alliance (Shin Saw Gyi of Sagaing to Kyawswa II) brought "no discernible benefit".

wars.name: Maw Shan raids on Sagaing and Pinya
wars.outcome: "Maw troops also breached northern Sagaing territory in 1342 but they were driven back"; raids in 1356-57, 1358-59 and 1362-63 "overran the entire Sagaing countryside"; "In April 1364, Maw forces broke through, and entered the city" and the Maw sacked Pinya in May.
wars.note: No Shan land was added. In 1363-64 the Maw laid siege to Sagaing "in early 1364, with Pinya forces enacting a naval blockade".

wars.name: Thado Minbya's conquest of Pinya
wars.outcome: "In September 1364, Thado Minbya seized Pinya, and claimed himself king of Sagaing and Pinya"; Ava was founded in 1365.
wars.note: Thado Minbya was Saw Yun's descendant (the page calls him both grandson and great-grandson) and Thihapate's stepson.

certainty.note: No surveyed or treaty border; Sagaing "claimed all the way to the border of Manipur" but its effective control "may have been no more than half today's Sagaing Region", and the only governor-level ruler named in its districts is at Tagaung.

notes: Cliopatria's Sagaing Kingdom (1326-1374) is one 345-cell outline in two identical shapes (1326, 1363) that, with Pinya's 324 cells, tile the 672-cell Myinsaing/Pinya/Ava outline. The row starts ten years after the page's 1315 and runs ten years past the page's 1365 (the Cliopatria Ava row begins in 1375, so 1365-1374 should be drawn by ava-kingdom). Corrections: a 1315-1325 keyframe (autonomous, contested with Pinya 1315-1317, nominal vassal of Pinya 1317-1325 per the Pinya ledger), a 1364-1365 keyframe for the union with Pinya, end moved from 1374 to 1365. The 1317-1325 vassal status is my reading of 'fought for autonomy in 1315-17' and 'formally seceded in 1325'. Open items: the page gives no area; the 345-cell outline is about twice the 'half of Sagaing Region' effective-control estimate and is kept as the claim; the founding date is 1315 on the lead and infobox but 26 March 1316 on the inscription footnote and 1322-23 in earlier chronicles; the page calls Thado Minbya both Saw Yun's grandson and great-grandson; no Mongol or Ming relation is on either page; the page budget (1-2 pages) was spent on Sagaing Kingdom and Pinya Kingdom. Whether Toungoo returned to Thado Minbya's realm in 1364 is not on the page; the 1364 keyframe leaves it out. The Pinya dossier carries the matching 1364 loss and the 1317 and 1325 vassal events.
